subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Proxy Voting and Activism
description: A fast breakdown of Proxy Voting and Activism for builders.

hook.text: You own stock in a company but can't attend the annual meeting. Your proxy vote is your voice.

buildup.text: Proxy voting lets shareholders vote on board members, executive pay, and corporate proposals remotely.

discovery.text: Activist investors buy large stakes and use proxy fights to force changes in strategy or leadership.

twist.text: Most retail investors never vote their proxies. Institutions and activists dominate shareholder democracy.

climax.text: Proxy voting is the core of shareholder democracy. But only those who use it have a voice.

punchline.text: Your shares, your vote. Most shareholders never use it.

quiz.question: What do activist investors use proxy fights for?
options: To force changes in company strategy or leadership
To sell their shares at a premium
To avoid paying taxes on gains
